body:
[A590] TAKEN
Branch: `640-m5`, local, from dev `e8454e2751d05b02ee8e5a571857589ab358ab86`.
Authoritative references: [assignment](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-6098404907); `docs/design/MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md` L8 and the ledger; owner decisions [5991591637](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5991591637), [5993114362](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5993114362) and [6081706413](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-6081706413); manager rulings D1, D3 and D7 ([5990755268](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5990755268)); REQ-CSR-01 to 04; `docs/reference/REGISTER_MAP.md`; `docs/testing/PP_SHADOW_BASELINE_RECIPE.md`; `docs/design/AREA_BUDGET.md`.
Interpreted scope: Restructure only the read path in `hdl/common/csr/milan_csr.sv`: the live-status read mux, the window read mux, the staged read-data path and the read-side snapshots. The goal is fewer LUTs. Every address, width, reset value, access semantic and snapshot coherence contract stays bit-identical. If the AXI-Lite read latency changes, I will state the bound and keep it inside the existing valid/ready contract. There is no port or parameter change. Both placement faces (all-fabric and `--ctrl-mailbox`) therefore instantiate the same block, and no split-interface logic is touched. I measure the current block first (out of context, and its share of the base route). The target is about 600 LUTs (400-1,000). I STOP if a register-map change looks necessary.
Validation plan:
- A lockstep bench of the new read path against a frozen copy of the current one, under random AXI traffic and random live inputs.
- Four planted defects, each failing a named check: a wrong decode, a torn multi-word snapshot, a stale snapshot after an update, and a reset-value drift.
- The `csr`, `tcam_csr` and `milan_dp` suites, the firmware host tests and the register-map checks, in both shapes and both placements.
- Lint and the repository gates the change touches.
- The M0s integrated route, base and candidate, run serially under the exclusive lock, then `pp_resource_gate.py check --endpoint route-1x1`. Every endpoint must pass and WNS must sit at or above the floor, with no exception added.
- Re-record only if all of that holds; D7 keeps the record until M9.
Blockers: none. M0s step 1 (parent integration) stops the selected-split route, so only the all-fabric route can be measured. I will show split-face parity by elaboration identity.
